title: Morphology of Non-Commercial Chitosan Films with and without Propolis: SEM Analysis
content: Chitosan is a natural biopolymer derived from the deacetylation of chitin, known for its unique properties such as biocompatibility, biodegradability, and antimicrobial activity. These characteristics have made it a widely used material in the production of thin films for applications in fields such as biomedical, pharmaceutical, and food industries (1). An innovative strategy to enhance the properties of chitosan is the incorporation of propolis, a natural product of bee origin known for its composition rich in flavonoids, phenols, and other bioactive compounds with potent antimicrobial, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory activities (2). The synergistic combination of chitosan and propolis properties opens new possibilities for the design of advanced materials with a sustainable and efficient approach (3). The objective of this study was to evaluate a non-commercial chitosan, obtained from shrimp shells, to produce films and their subsequent enrichment with propolis.
